Dubai's derivatives exchange DGCX is rebuilding its trading backbone with Tata Consultancy Services, a five-market upgrade announced this week.

بورصة دبي للذهب والسلع (DGCX) تعيد بناء بنيتها التقنية بالتعاون مع «تاتا كونسلتنسي سيرفيسز» (TCS)، في تطوير يشمل خمسة أسواق للمشتقات.

TCS runs DGCX's clearing, surveillance and connectivity on its BaNCS and Quartz platforms, across energy, currencies, equities, bullion and metals. It builds on June's Gold Spot T+0 Contract, DGCX's own first for same-day settled spot gold.

DGCX and TCS statements, 15 September; via Business Standard, ANI.

Dubai: gold pulled back to AED 503.86 a gram (24K) this morning, down 1.85% on the tape's own board, still an intraday reading before New York's close settles.

دبي: تراجع الذهب إلى 503.86 درهمًا لعيار 24 هذا الصباح، بانخفاض 1.85% وفق تعرفة الصحيفة، وهي قراءة لحظية قبل إقفال نيويورك.

22K stands at AED 461.88 a gram and silver at AED 7,430 a kilogram, both down with the metal itself (gold spot $4,267.30/oz, silver $62.93/oz via Kitco, AED/USD 3.6725 peg).
